A1.justification: Both PDFs contain the same research work, with 38 readable pages including supplementary Sections 1–10. Text and rendered-page comparisons establish that differences are confined to the arXiv stamp on page 1 and the acknowledgment and spacing on page 15.

before.justification: v1 reports original DPT and Sparse Merging experiments on JRDB and JTA, including main Tables 1–4, plus robustness studies and Bench2Drive experiments in the supplement.

after.justification: v2 retains the same original experimental results, including the JRDB/JTA comparisons, three-seed robustness results and Bench2Drive evaluation.

M1.justification: The architecture, losses, disjoint-mask training in Algorithm 1, Sparse Merging and additional joint-reasoning stage are unchanged. The supplementary HiP-AD adaptation is also identical.

E1.justification: Both versions retain the same JRDB/JTA crowd prediction and planning coverage, dense-scene and prediction-subtask scenarios, and Bench2Drive vehicle-domain perception and planning evaluation.

E2.justification: Main Table 4 retains DIPP, DTPP, Ensemble, Task Arithmetic, Ties Merging, Localize-and-Stitch and T-Switch. Corresponding supplementary comparisons also retain the same methods, including PCGrad, CAGrad, VAD, UniAD, DriveTransformer and HiP-AD.

E3.justification: Data splits, preprocessing, training budgets, model configurations and evaluation procedures are unchanged. These include the 9-step observation/12-step prediction protocol at 2.5 fps and the supplementary Dev10 closed-loop and open-loop evaluation.

E4.justification: The allocation and sparsity sweeps, capacity and scheduling sensitivity studies, controlled-overlap experiments, subtask decomposition, mask evolution, layer analyses and qualitative cases are identical in the main text and supplementary Sections 5–6.

E5.justification: Supplementary Section 6.3 and Table 4 retain the same three-seed evaluation and standard-deviation reporting. No run counts, uncertainty estimates or statistical procedures are added or revised.

E6.justification: All numerical results and qualitative findings are unchanged. For example, main Table 4 retains DPT + SM planning/prediction ADE values of 0.4044/0.5952 on JRDB, and supplementary Table 12 retains HiP-AD + DPT + SM route completion of 95.95 and driving score of 86.57.

T1.justification: The task-vector, activation-mask, overlap and merging definitions in Section 3, along with supplementary loss and metric formulas, are identical. No assumptions, mathematical reasoning or proofs are added or revised.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same claims about Skill Conflict, DPT, Sparse Merging and their benefits for compact unified prediction and planning models.

C2.justification: Interpretations of parameter interference, capacity effects and training/inference tradeoffs are unchanged. Supplementary Section 10 retains the same qualifications concerning broader task grouping and adaptive hyperparameter selection.

D1.justification: Dataset preparation, hyperparameters, hardware, training costs, inference measurements, checkpoint information and the project-page link are unchanged. The added NVIDIA grant acknowledgment provides no new implementation or resource-access details.

R1.justification: Related work, novelty positioning and both reference lists are identical. No cited works or relationships to prior research are added or removed.

P1.justification: Page 15 adds the sentence 'Research supported by the NVIDIA Academic Grant Program.' The arXiv stamp changes from v1 dated 22 July 2026 to v2 dated 27 August 2026; research prose and section organization remain unchanged.

P2.justification: Page 15 has small vertical-spacing adjustments around the conclusion, acknowledgments and references to accommodate the added funding credit. The marginal stamp changes on page 1; all figures, tables, captions and supplementary layouts remain identical.

improvement.justification: v2 adds a funding acknowledgment and updates the version stamp, with minor spacing adjustments. The methods, evidence, explanations and reproducibility information remain identical throughout the main paper and supplement, so these administrative edits do not materially change overall paper quality.
